observations: Photo 0 shows two motherboards stacked vertically on a concrete block.
The top motherboard has a CPU cooler installed, with visible heat pipes and a fan.
Both boards have similar layouts: multiple RAM slots, PCIe slots, and I/O ports on the back.
The I/O panel on the bottom board shows USB ports (including blue USB 3.0), audio jacks, and PS/2 ports.
The top board has a green and white sticker near the bottom left, possibly a brand or model label, but it is too blurry to read.
The boards appear used, with some dust and minor wear.
No visible branding or model numbers are legible on either board.
The socket area is covered by the cooler on the top board; the bottom board's socket is not visible.

claims.evidence: No visible branding or model number to confirm generation. The photo does not show the chipset or any clear identifier.
The presence of a CPU cooler suggests a CPU is installed, but the processor type is not visible. The socket is covered, and no model is readable to confirm compatibility.
The socket is not visible on either board. The I/O panel and layout are consistent with LGA 1150 boards, but this is not definitive without seeing the socket or reading the model.

risks.risk: The motherboard may not be compatible with 4th generation Intel processors or may be a different generation.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the model label or chipset, or a close-up of the socket area.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic used motherboard without generation-specific value

risks.risk: The motherboard may be damaged or non-functional (e.g., missing components, bent pins, or power issues).
risks.proof: A video showing the board powered on with a working CPU and RAM, or a close-up of the socket and VRM area.

risks.risk: The boards may be counterfeit or repurposed (e.g., old boards relabeled).
risks.proof: A photo of the model label or serial number, or a close-up of the PCB with manufacturer markings.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified, with lower value

proof_requests: Clear photo of the model label or chipset on the motherboard.
Close-up of the CPU socket area (if possible without the cooler).
Photo of the PCB with any manufacturer or serial number markings.
Video of the board powering on with a CPU and RAM installed.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a motherboard, but critical details like model, generation, and socket type are unreadable. Without proof of compatibility with 4th gen Intel processors and socket 1150, the item cannot be priced accurately. Hidden risks include non-functionality and misrepresentation.
